items.Y_desc: Score from 0 (clean, rendered text) to 10 (pervasive unrendered LaTeX commands, stray hyphens, or copy-paste artifacts such as a placeholder). Measure only the extent of formatting artifacts; do not judge whether they harm readability.

items.X_desc: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the abstract use terminology associated with currently prominent ML themes or application agendas? Judge only topical vocabulary, not whether the work is good.
items.Y_desc: Rate 0-10 the extent to which the abstract contains period-specific benchmarks, older model families, dated citations, or language signaling a particular research era; judge only temporal cues, not whether the work is current or valuable.

items.X_desc: On a 0-10 scale, rate how LONG this abstract is relative to a typical conference abstract (0 = a few words/title-only, 10 = maximally long and dense with clauses). Score only extent of length, not whether the length is appropriate or the writing is good.
items.Y_desc: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the abstract contain dated benchmarks, named annual events, software versions, or other era-specific identifiers? Judge only visible temporal markers, not whether the work is good.

items.X_desc: Rate the extent to which the abstract explicitly frames itself as fixing, relieving, or responding to 'existing methods', 'previous works', or 'recent attempts'. Do not judge if the response is valid.
items.Y_desc: Score from 0 (self-contained problem with no reference to prior methods) to 10 (the abstract explicitly frames itself against many existing baselines or prior limitations). Score only the degree of crowded-conversation framing; do not judge whether the positioning is accurate.

items.X_desc: Rate 0-10 how much this abstract contains an explicit mention of released code, a GitHub link, or a project webpage (e.g. 'Code is available at...', 'alfworld.github.io'). 0 = no such mention, 10 = prominent explicit link/boilerplate. Do not judge whether releasing code is good practice.
items.Y_desc: Score from 0 (no URL or repository mentioned) to 10 (explicit URL plus statement of public code or data availability). Score only the presence and prominence of links; do not judge whether the resources are good.

items.X_desc: Rate 0-10 how much this entry consists only of a title (and possibly a one-line fragment like 'International audience') with no substantive abstract body. 0 = full abstract present, 10 = title/stub only with essentially no body text. This is a mechanical completeness check, not a quality judgement.
items.Y_desc: Rate 0-10 how much prose, subordinate clauses, and distinct contribution or result claims are packed into the abstract; judge only extent, not whether the claims are good or high quality.

items.X_desc: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the abstract include exact numerical gains, benchmark values, resource savings, or named performance thresholds? Judge only quantity of numerical reporting, not whether the work is good.
items.Y_desc: Rate 0-10 the extent of displayed mathematics, symbolic notation, theorem-style language, and technical formalism; judge only extent, not whether the formalism is correct or valuable.

items.X_desc: Rate 0-10 the extent to which the abstract introduces capitalized method, model, dataset, or loss names and acronym expansions; judge only naming prevalence, not whether the names are useful.
items.Y_desc: Score from 0 (no novel acronyms or coined method names) to 10 (multiple invented acronyms such as SSFG or Fixup). Count only new proper-noun method labels; do not judge whether the names are well-chosen.

items.X_name: Numeric-result specificity: explicit percentages and deltas
items.X_desc: Score 0-10 how much of the text consists of explicit quantitative outcome statements — percentage figures, point deltas, speed-up multipliers, scores given to one or more decimals. 0 = no numbers reported at all; 10 = many precise figures, deltas and multipliers stated throughout. Score only the amount and precision of numeric reporting present in the text; do not judge whether the numbers are impressive, correct, or well-supported.
items.Y_desc: Score from 0 (no mathematical symbols or formalism) to 10 (dense with inline symbols, norms, sets, and equations). Score only the amount of mathematical notation visible in the text; do not judge whether the math is correct.

items.X_desc: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the abstract use priority, novelty, superiority, record, or unusually strong self-promotional wording? Judge only presence of such rhetoric, not whether the work is good.
items.Y_desc: Rate 0-10 how much prose, subordinate clauses, and distinct contribution or result claims are packed into the abstract; judge only extent, not whether the claims are good or high quality.

items.X_desc: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the abstract contain dated benchmarks, named annual events, software versions, or other era-specific identifiers? Judge only visible temporal markers, not whether the work is good.
items.Y_desc: Rate 0-10 the extent to which the abstract advertises code, data, videos, project pages, repositories, or other immediately accessible artifacts; judge only the presence and prominence of these signals, not their usefulness.

items.X_desc: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the abstract foreground named authors, papers, systems, or explicit comparative lineage? Judge only visible citation-style density, not whether the work is good.
items.Y_desc: Rate 0-10 the extent to which the abstract contains period-specific benchmarks, older model families, dated citations, or language signaling a particular research era; judge only temporal cues, not whether the work is current or valuable.

anchors.X_name: Presence of a trailing signature block
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for how fully the text ends with a personal sign-off: a name, initials, a handle, or a closing salutation. Extent only.
anchors.Y_name: Author sign-off at the end of the text
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for whether the writer closes by naming or initialling themselves. Extent only; do not judge quality.

anchors.X_name: How much displayed mathematics the text contains
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the density of set-off equation blocks. Count only; do not judge whether the mathematics is correct.
anchors.Y_name: How much the text hedges its own claims
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for the frequency of 'I think', 'perhaps', 'it seems' and similar. Count only; do not judge whether the hedging is warranted.
